analysis.title: International Market Intelligence: Morning Briefing (October 27, 2026)
key_insights: Revival of the AI trade lifted markets broadly on 10/26 and carried into Asia, but there is no full return to risk-on. Few investors have an incentive to take big risks ahead of a heavy event week. Khuram stays on Quality over Risk.

Market Intelligence has held since August that tech should be traded with balanced thematic/factor exposure: longs and shorts across AI Infra (Inference), Capex Spenders (Hyperscalers) and Vulnerables (AI-resilient Software), not a large Semis vs. Software trade. The view is not changed because monetization concerns, which cause the financing bottleneck, are unresolved.

Technicals are supportive and JPM is open to a tactical bounce in AI infra before year-end. Positioning, sentiment and factor signals are starting to show bottoming. The SOX vs. SPX drawdown now rivals 2008, which suggests tech may be under-pricing the length of the capex cycle.

IPO news, META financing and AVGO/SPCX deals make it less likely that capex is cut materially for lack of financing. De-grossing has been driven mostly by thematic beta rather than beta to fundamentals/capex. Powering AI and some industrial names could outperform on a rebound.

Diplomatic efforts to ease Middle East tensions helped at the margin. The absence of a Moody's downgrade on France helped stabilize intra-EMU spreads and SX7E. Brazil vs. MXEF P/E is still high after repricing.

EU equity strategy: French sentiment is already very downbeat. The CAC40 has underperformed in a straight line for 3 years and its relative P/E is at record lows. A budget likely passing in 1-2 months is a small positive and a centrist candidate could emerge. JPM expects an OW non-French domestic vs French pair trade to keep working over the medium term.

EU quant strategy: the QMI rotated into Contraction in June with long Quality / short Risk. Over three months Quality (RoE, low leverage) is +6.6% long/short and Risk (beta/vol/estimate-risk) is -8.4%. The QMI keeps its contraction call, seeing early stages of a rotation toward balance sheet strength and profitability.

Asia data centers: the power-market impact varies by market and Malaysia has the largest potential incremental demand. In India, long-term C&I renewable PPAs give exposure, with CleanMax a direct beneficiary. Malaysia's approval framework and grid needs support Tenaga and YTL Power. In China, green-power demand could help renewable operators.

ASEAN's next decade: the most durable AI upside comes from adoption at scale, operating model redesign, workforce readiness and data governance, more than from data centers and semiconductors. Trade reconfiguration benefits ASEAN but returns vary by country.
APAC client sentiment is more bearish than in the US and somewhat less than in the EU. APAC clients are up double digits on the year, so many lack incentive to re-engage until a clear trend emerges.

US consumer is robust. The top 4 income quintiles hold 6%-27% more inflation-adjusted cash than at YE2019, nearly $8T in nominal terms. Retail sales run $723bn/month YTD2026 vs $505bn in 2019. Card delinquencies and charge-offs are normalizing to pre-COVID trends, not deteriorating. HY defaults are 2.7% vs a 3.2% long-term average.

Consumer sub-sectors: airlines, cruise and hotels show robust demand. Autos and homebuilders are rate-sensitive, so parts and suppliers may be better expressions. Retailers face freight costs of 30-40% of total cost, with rates more than tripled YTD. Staples are seen as most at risk of margin compression and a likely source of funds.

AI credit: markets are becoming more discriminating on AI infra but there is no sign of a broader funding crisis. AI infrastructure has absorbed over $500B of debt YTD (IG >$350B, leveraged >$60B, private credit ~$100B+). Hyperscaler all-in funding costs are up about 120bps. The HY compute index is +372bps YTD. Leveraged GPU and data center developers face rising financing constraints.

AI-related CDS spreads have widened on technical selling and bank hedging of data center lending rather than fundamentals. CDS now trades above cash-bond spreads for some names, which makes selling protection attractive. CRWV, which also has converts outstanding, trades at a slightly positive basis.

IG TMT credit: MSFT, GOOGL and AMZN spreads have held up while externally financed names, especially Oracle, have underperformed. ORCL and SpaceX widened on reports each is seeking off-balance-sheet financing. Rising debt supply may pressure spreads into 2027. Nvidia is a key transmission channel for financial stress given its ties to GPU customers including CRWV.

HY TMT credit: CRWV has a financing challenge, not a solvency one. Analyst Tom Egan projects CRWV last-12-month EBITDA rising from ~$4.4B in June 2026 to $7.3B by YE and nearly $20B by YE27. CRWV has ~$130B of contracted revenue commitments and potential access to equity, customer-supported financing and SPVs.

France/Europe contagion fears are viewed as exaggerated. France has a ~3% primary deficit and debt/GDP of c.120%, and debt/GDP above 180% is the typical Rubicon, 10-15 years away on unchanged policy. Italy could stabilize its debt with ~50bp of spending cuts vs >300bp for France. The ECB backstop (TPI, OMT, PEPP flexibility) limits the risk of disorderly spread widening. JPM sees a France-specific story, not a sovereign crisis 2.0.

French equities: Exporters and Domestics are both shorted, which makes France a funder at the country level. Drivers are geopolitics/tariffs for exporters and fiscal concerns for domestics. French bonds: the selloff was worsened by HF crowding in carry proxies and ~60% non-resident ownership. OATs discount debt/GDP above 150% and an implied deficit above 8%. JPM sees room for relief into year-end around the budget but no material reversal before elections in 2Q27.

EU banks: the tape echoes the 2011-12 sovereign crisis, but JPM sees the earnings trend as unchanged and says dips of more than 15% vs. the index should be bought. Call ratio spreads and call spreads are attractive.

Midterms: federal AI regulation is unlikely because Trump would veto and Democrats cannot reach a 2/3 majority. If Democrats take the House they could defund Middle East military efforts. Tariff policy is unlikely to change. Longer-dated bonds could see a bid if Democrats halt deficit spending.

Treasuries: before the 10/22 rally JPM's view was that a 10-year yield of 5.50% was more likely than 5.00%. The market prices a Dec 2026 hike and two in FY27. Clients see upside risk to that path. The downside risk is a near-term end to the US/Iran conflict and a quick normalization of oil and shipping costs, held with low conviction.

AI/tech client pushback: semis revenue is driven by supply-chain price spikes unsustainable in a DCF, neoclouds face contagion and bankruptcy risk (hyperscalers would likely buy cheaply), and software is unlikely to be a source of funds. Security and infra software are consensus longs. The buy trigger is a positioning flush, hyperscaler capex confirmation, semis earnings, tighter credit and seasonality, pointing to early November.

Broadening: since the July 28 lows the SPX is +4.8% through 10/22, but more than half the index has a negative return and 69% of stocks lag the SPX. An 'everything rally' can work short term but not longer term, with tech dominating once the market stabilizes. About 65% of SPX companies cited AI operating improvement in 26Q2 earnings, but fewer than 5% quantified it.

Cyclicals and other assets: clients favor financials (GSIBs, card issuers), see aero/defense negatively given a possible Blue Wave halting military funding, and view industrials as an AI play. Funding shorts for tech could combine consumer, healthcare, smid caps and Europe. The dollar is seen range-bound with a local high likely in, gold is interesting after its decline, and copper is a bull case tied to a China growth reboot.

Mkt Intel is tactically bullish on global equities, long US and Asia (Japan, Korea, Taiwan) vs. EU. Longs: tech and supercycle themes, EU and JA banks, EU industrials, JA machinery, GE Infra, EU miners, EU pharma, UKX and selective consumer. Shorts: AI-vulnerable ex-software, short-cycle data center capex names, EU insurance, autos, chemicals, Asian consumer electronics, MedTech and MDAX. Option hedges: MCX < UKX and short FR vs EU domestics.

EM monetization: EM has recovered over 9% of its drawdown since the end-July bottom. JPM is bullish on EM and favors tactical longs in China Star 50 vs KWEB, Korea vs South East Asia, and Taiwan. Hedges include long Brazil (EWZ) ahead of the second-round presidential vote and EM (EEM) for broadening exposure.

Positioning: hedge funds are -3.3% MTD globally vs SPX +0.2% MTD, so alpha rather than beta drove the drawdown. Eq L/S 20d alpha (-2.9%) is the worst since Feb 2021. CTAs have sold US equities every day since 10/13, led by Nasdaq. Retail remained net buyer at the slowest pace in a year, and ETFs bought, led by tech.

Flows: combined ETF, retail and HF 60d relative flows into Info Tech are near record highs (+3z). Flows into Utilities, Real Estate and Materials are at or near extreme lows. Healthcare is the defensive exception. Stabilization signs: Eq L/S net leverage at 12m and 3yr lows, Multi-Strat de-grossing slowing, quants re-grossing. Risks: gross leverage is still high (77th percentile 12m), Eq L/S alpha is still falling, and CTAs could sell more.

earnings_insights: Earnings calendar: 10/28 GOOG, MSFT, UBS, DBL, SAN, BNP, STAN. 10/29 AMZN, INTC, EU Banks (incl. GLE). All dates are upcoming and no results are reported.
Of SPX companies, ~65% cited AI operating improvement in 26Q2 earnings but fewer than 5% quantified the impact.
Recent airline, cruise and hotel earnings releases and management commentary confirmed robust demand despite higher prices.
JPM credit analyst Tom Egan projects CRWV last-12-month EBITDA of ~$4.4B in June 2026, $7.3B by YE2026 and nearly $20B by YE2027. These are forecasts.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Clients see upside risk to this path. Fed DOTS show no hikes in FY27, which many consider unlikely.

macro_indicators.reading: 5.50% more likely than 5.00% before the Oct 22 rally
macro_indicators.interpretation: Higher rates favor Quality and hurt businesses built for low rates.
Corporate sector health argues against a near-term recession.
Spending is robust and higher energy prices are not crowding out discretionary spending.
OATs discount debt/GDP above 150% and a deficit above 8%, which JPM sees as excessive.
Key event in a heavy catalyst week alongside ECB 10/29 and BOJ 10/30.

risk_factors: Monetization concerns for AI remain unresolved and are causing a financing bottleneck.
Growing AI debt issuance, interconnected finance arrangements, higher borrowing costs and delivery of compute capacity on schedule.
Neocloud turmoil could spread across the group and bankruptcy risk exists.
Nvidia credit support and circular financing create concentration and correlated downside risk.
French politics (far-right victory as polling base case) and fiscal concerns could pressure EGB spreads.
Eq L/S alpha is still deteriorating, CTAs could sell more and retail demand is soft.
Rate hikes could exceed market pricing given strong balance sheets and inflation.
Higher freight costs and rates for retailers, and margin compression for staples.
Semis revenue driven by supply-chain price spikes is unsustainable in a DCF.

vol_and_positioning: Hedge funds are -3.3% MTD globally (from -2.1% the prior week) vs SPX +0.2% MTD and ACWI -1.0%. YTD HF returns are +4.7%, down from +6%.
Eq L/S 20d alpha of -2.9% is the worst since Feb 2021. Multi-Strat alpha is the worst since Aug 2024. 60d crowding returns of -4.1% are back to July 2024 levels.
HF net flows were -0.9z. Multi-Strat 5d gross fell -0.9% vs -3.3% a week ago. Quants kept adding gross (80th percentile).
CTAs' US equity exposure has fallen every day since 10/13, led by Nasdaq. Exposure is only ~45th percentile LT so they could sell more.
US TPM is at the 28th percentile, Europe the 8th, and China/HK at -2z. Eq L/S net leverage is at 12m and 3yr lows, with gross leverage still at the 77th percentile 12m and 95th 5yr.
AI Core Revenue and Semis positioning fell to the 94th percentile LT from 99th.
Hedging ideas: call ratio spreads and call spreads on EU Banks, and long MCX < UKX.
geopolitical: Diplomatic efforts to ease Middle East tensions helped markets at the margin.
EU plans more import curbs on China in early 2027.
Possible near-term end to the US/Iran conflict is the main downside risk to the rate-hike pricing.
Brazil's second-round presidential election is at the end of the month.
US Secretary of State hosts a two-day G20 Foreign Ministers' Meeting on 10/30.
If Democrats take the House in the midterms they could defund Middle East military efforts.

tension_points.bull_case: SOX vs. SPX drawdown rivals 2008, positioning, sentiment and factor signals show bottoming, and financing announcements reduce the risk of capex cuts.
tension_points.bear_case: Monetization concerns remain unresolved and are causing a financing bottleneck, so JPM does not change its fundamental view.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A buy needs a positioning flush, hyperscaler capex confirmation, semis earnings, tighter credit and positive seasonality, which JPM says points to early November.

tension_points.bull_case: Hyperscalers are fundamentally strong, capital remains available, and CDS widening is technical and not fundamental.
tension_points.bear_case: Leveraged GPU and data center developers face financing constraints, growing debt supply may pressure spreads into 2027, and circular Nvidia financing adds correlated risk.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Rising rates and larger required equity contributions for leveraged GPU financing.

tension_points.bull_case: Debt/GDP is far below the 180% threshold, the ECB backstop limits disorderly widening, and a budget passing could bring year-end relief.
tension_points.bear_case: Political backdrop is challenging, a far-right victory is the polling base case, and the tape echoes 2011-12.
tension_points.what_invalidates: JPM does not call a material reversal until the 2Q27 elections.

tension_points.bull_case: Crowding returns are low, Multi-Strat de-grossing has slowed, quants are re-grossing and ETFs are buying the dip.
tension_points.bear_case: Eq L/S alpha is still falling, gross leverage is high and retail demand is soft.
tension_points.what_invalidates: CTAs, at roughly the 45th percentile LT US exposure, could sell further if markets do not rebound.
